michael: Heads-up — after enabling the interleaved mixed-quant kernels on canary, our codegen eval suite shows a ~2.4% drop in schema-match and some structured output breakage. Also seeing a ~10% p50->p95 tail increase on longctx runs. Repro steps below. :eyes:

anya: Which layers got FP8 vs INT4? calibration method?

michael: Interleaved pattern: FP8 on attention layers 0-7, INT4 on FFN layers 8-23. Calibration: per-layer min/max from nightly batch (no per-seq-length reweight). Canary id: canary-2026-03-14-7.

sanjay: Can you paste the profiler slices? Also any signs of KV cache dtype casts or extra memcpy? I've seen mixed-dtype serialization blow up tail latencies.

michael: Quick top stacks from perf sample (canary host):

```
# pprof snippet
50%  runtime  quantize_ff
20%  runtime  dequantize_kv + memcpy
10%  runtime  aten::matmul
8%   runtime  kv_serialize
12%  other
```

michael: Note `dequantize_kv + memcpy` time spikes when there's a big burst of cached seqs.

lee: @michael can you also share the cached-kv header bytes? If we serialized as int8 but deserialize expecting fp16 we get subtle numerical drift.

michael: Put a sample header (hex) in the repo gist but short version: `kv_meta: {dtype: int8, quant: perlayer}`.

tess: I ran a small reproducible on my laptop: disabling INT4 on the final output projection layer makes schema-match go back to baseline. So seems sensitive to precision at projection->softmax boundary.

anya: That matches a theory: output projection quant noise amplifies, early tokens go off-distribution and break structured output parsing. We should treat output projection layers as 'sensitive' in kernel-selection.

sanjay: Short-term mitigations:
- Add a KV deserialization sanity check that verifies dtype header vs expected model config (fast fail).
- Add a kernel-selection guard: force FP8 for layers marked `sensitive` (output proj / value heads).
- Add a regression gate to the canary rollout: if schema-match delta > 1% or tail latency +8% trigger rollback.

michael: Sounds good. @anya can you run a calibration sweep where we re-compute scales using stratified samples by sequence length? I suspect current calibration optimized for short seqs.

anya: On it — I'll run 3 calibration configs (default, seq-weighted, per-batch) and post deltas. ETA: 12h.

lee: I'll hold the canary and flip traffic off for canary-2026-03-14-7 until we have a fix. Also adding an alert to catch KV dtype mismatches.

dev-bot: Rollout action: `canary-2026-03-14-7` paused by @lee at 1759999999.

michael: Action items pinned: @anya calibration sweep, @sanjay add KV sanity check + kernel guard, @lee hold & alert. I'll produce a regression report and attach eval diffs to the ticket.

tess: Quick note: we should also add a unit test that exercises schema-check on tiny prompts with mixed-quant kernels to catch this in CI.

michael: +1. I'll add the test checklist. Once we have the calibration + guards, we can try a conservative canary with 1% traffic.

sanjay: If anyone needs a reproducer, I put a small harness in `eng-runtime/tools/mq-repro/README.md` — run `./repro --canary canary-2026-03-14-7 --seed 42`.

michael: Thanks all. Will update thread with eval diffs and perf plots when available. :thumbsup:
